title: coptosperma sessiliflorum
intro: Coptosperma sessiliflorum, commonly known as the Ceylon tea bush or the green tea of the forest, is a plant species native to tropical Africa and Southeast Asia. It has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, which include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties that help to boost the immune system and protect against various diseases. The therapeutic actions of Coptosperma sessiliflorum are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids that have been shown to exhibit anti-cancer, anti-diabetic, and anti-hypertensive effects. The bioactive constituents of Coptosperma sessiliflorum have been found to include flavonoids such as quercetin and kaempferol, phenolic acids like ferulic acid and sinapic acid, and terpenoids including limonene and beta-pinene.
